source_decisions.reason: Publication or revision timing cannot be fully established; retain only as explicitly uncertain evidence.

observations.observation: Axios reported from unnamed sources that OpenAI's annualized run rate was nearing $70B, up more than 70% since Q3 began; business-to-business revenue had more than doubled since July, and Q3 consumer revenue additions exceeded those for all of 2025.
observations.event_time: Q3 2026 through Sep. 29, 2026; the report does not specify the exact measurement date
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: This is an anonymous-source report of a run rate, not reported full-year revenue or a company filing. Axios said it did not have OpenAI expense details.

observations.observation: Before the new report, Bloomberg Law had reported an OpenAI annualized run rate above $40B; Axios's Sep. 3 context also cited an above-$40B figure and warned that OpenAI and Anthropic revenue comparisons were affected by differing treatment of cloud-partner sales.
observations.event_time: Prior reporting in August and September 2026; underlying run-rate measurement dates are not specified precisely
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The earlier figures were also reported run rates, not audited results; the different accounting treatment cautions against treating headline comparisons as directly equivalent.

observations.observation: A Bloomberg search result indicates near-cutoff pickup of the Axios report at approximately 14:41 UTC, but its headline explicitly credits Axios and does not establish independent sourcing.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The page fetch was restricted and no dated pre-cutoff snapshot or update history was verified; use only as a search-result dissemination trace.

observations.observation: Inference from the report's scope: this is an AI-services revenue and enterprise-adoption signal, not a disclosed Micron result or a direct fact about memory purchases, HBM/DRAM content, or hardware spending.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The report does not identify Micron or quantify an effect on memory demand.

gaps: No official OpenAI filing, company confirmation, realized full-year revenue, or expense/profit breakdown supporting the near-$70B run-rate claim was located before cutoff.
No independently sourced confirmation of the Sep. 29 figure before cutoff was verified; the Bloomberg search result is downstream of Axios, and the full page could not be checked.
No direct link from this report to Micron memory orders, memory content, supplier allocation, or a Micron operating metric was found.
No separate same-day Micron or memory-market development was independently verified in this focused search.
research_notes: The earliest traceable public report located is Axios on Sep. 29 at 14:15:40 UTC, before the 14:46:20 UTC cutoff. The supplied feed item’s timestamp (14:43:04 UTC) is later and appears to restate that report. Bloomberg search metadata shows a Sep. 29 item at 14:41 UTC, but its headline attributes the report to Axios; it is a dissemination trace, not independent confirmation. The reported figure is an annualized run rate sourced to unnamed people, not an official OpenAI financial disclosure. Prior reporting placed OpenAI above a $40B annualized run rate and cautioned that comparisons with Anthropic were affected by different cloud-partner revenue accounting. No direct Micron, memory procurement, or hardware-spending fact was identified in the triggering report.
